ipad-pro.evidence: Apple lists a built-in rechargeable lithium-polymer battery and up to 10 hours of web browsing or video playback.

kindle.evidence: Amazon's Kindle Paperwhite listing describes weeks of battery life; actual results vary with use, wireless settings and light level.

codex-1.evidence: Concept claim for the paper-first object; no production unit or test report exists yet.

ipad-pro.evidence: iPadOS ships with built-in apps and access to the App Store, so the device is not limited to reading.

kindle.evidence: Amazon positions Kindle as a dedicated reading device; this is a product-category description, not a measured attention test.

codex-1.evidence: Bookln design intent. No feed, notifications or general-purpose app surface is planned.

ipad-pro.evidence: Apple lists a glass-fronted Ultra Retina XDR display with a nano-texture glass option. No drop-test comparison is claimed.

kindle.evidence: Amazon describes Kindle Paperwhite as a glare-free e-reader. Bookln has not tested drop performance.

codex-1.evidence: Concept claim. Structural and drop testing must be completed before any durability statement is published.

ipad-pro.evidence: Apps are installed and opened through iPadOS and the App Store.

kindle.evidence: Kindle devices provide built-in reading tools and access to Amazon's Kindle store.

codex-1.evidence: Concept capability. The page-edge mark and companion layer are represented by the deterministic knowledge-graph preview.

ipad-pro.evidence: Material description based on Apple's published enclosure and display materials.

kindle.evidence: Material description, not a measured tactile study.

codex-1.evidence: Concept art direction for the physical object.
